::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## The two models

| | **delta_SCM** (the original model; file `b1`) | **downstream_DOC** (the new parameterization; file `b1_downstream`) |
|---|---|---|
| Outcome | $\Delta\text{DOC} = \text{DOC}_{down} - \text{DOC}_{up}$ | $\text{DOC}_{down}$ |
| Measurement error on the outcome | 0.283 mg L$^{-1}$ (the two 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ errors propagated, $\sqrt{0.2^2+0.2^2}$) | 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ (one concentration) |
| Role of upstream DOC | predictor (standardized), *and* subtracted inside the outcome | predictor on the mg L$^{-1}$ scale, with a freely estimated **inheritance slope** (prior Normal(1, 0.3)) |
| Mediators, priors, site effect, Student-*t* likelihood, sampler | identical | identical |
| $\Delta\text{DOC}$ | is the outcome | is derived afterwards: predicted downstream DOC minus upstream DOC, per posterior draw |

Everything else — the DAG, the thirteen hypothesised paths, the data (360 samplings, 16 streams with producers) — is the same.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## The research question the SCM answers

**Q2 — Drivers.** *Which abiotic and biotic drivers set the direction of the local DOC change in beaver-engineered streams?* The SCM estimates the paths dams → water residence time → primary producers → DOC, solar radiation → producers → DOC, and litter → DOC, with upstream DOC as the incoming state. It does not answer Q1 (direction; paired-contrast model behind Figure 1a) or Q3 (magnitude; the four-concentration model behind $S$, $R_s$, $G$).
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Short answer

-   The two models are one likelihood written in two coordinate systems, and every mediator effect agrees to the second decimal (@tbl-equivalence).
-   Downstream DOC as the outcome gives upstream DOC one role (the inherited state, 0.95 mg per mg) and reads the mediators as what beaver-engineering *adds*; ΔDOC as the outcome measures the process directly but makes upstream DOC both a predictor and half of the response.
-   ΔDOC is recovered exactly from the downstream model for every stream and draw (@fig-ddoc), so nothing is lost either way — the choice is about which reading the manuscript wants to lead with.
:::

# 1. The DAG

```{r fig-dag}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "**The structural causal model of Q2, as fitted (downstream_DOC).** Downstream DOC inherits the upstream state (slope 0.95 mg per mg) and is modified by the hydrological and biological pathways; numbers are posterior mean standardized effects; solid blue: positive with posterior probability above 0.90; dashed grey: no-evidence. In delta_SCM the same graph has ΔDOC in place of downstream DOC and the upstream-DOC arrow carries −0.10 (standardized) instead of 0.95."
knitr::include_graphics(here("images", "Figure_1b_downstream.png"))
```

# 2. The two parameterizations are one model

**delta_SCM**, ΔDOC as the outcome, with mediators $M_k$ (macrophytes, phytoplankton, litter cover, water residence time) and a stream random intercept $u$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta\text{DOC}_i &= \text{DOC}_{down,i} - \text{DOC}_{up,i} \\
\Delta\text{DOC}_i &\sim \text{Student-}t\!\left(\nu,\; \mu^{\Delta}_i,\; \sigma\right) \\
\mu^{\Delta}_i &= \alpha + \beta_1\,\text{DOC}_{up,i} + \sum_k \beta_k M_{k,i} + u_{site(i)}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-delta}

**downstream_DOC**, downstream DOC as the outcome:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{DOC}_{down,i} &\sim \text{Student-}t\!\left(\nu,\; \mu_i,\; \sigma\right) \\
\mu_i &= \alpha' + \beta_{inh}\,\text{DOC}_{up,i} + \sum_k \beta'_k M_{k,i} + u'_{site(i)}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-down}

Subtracting $\text{DOC}_{up,i}$ from both sides of @eq-down gives

$$
\text{DOC}_{down,i} - \text{DOC}_{up,i} = \alpha' + (\beta_{inh} - 1)\,\text{DOC}_{up,i} + \sum_k \beta'_k M_{k,i} + u'_{site(i)} + \varepsilon_i ,
$$ {#eq-subtract}

which is @eq-delta with $\beta_1 = \beta_{inh} - 1$ (on the mg L$^{-1}$ scale; times the SD of upstream DOC, `r sprintf("%.2f", cmp$s_up)` mg L$^{-1}$, on the standardized scale), $\beta_k = \beta'_k$ and the same $\nu$, $\sigma$, $u$. The negative "effect of upstream DOC on ΔDOC" in delta_SCM ($\beta_1 < 0$) *is* the inheritance slope being slightly below one ($\beta_{inh} < 1$). The fitted models confirm it:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-equivalence
#| tbl-cap: "The same SCM fitted as delta_SCM (ΔDOC outcome) and downstream_DOC (downstream-DOC outcome). Posterior mean [95% credible interval]. The inheritance slope implied by delta_SCM is 1 + β₁/SD(upstream DOC)."
#| echo: false
q <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", mean(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
kable(tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~`delta_SCM: outcome ΔDOC`, ~`downstream_DOC: outcome downstream DOC`,
  "Inheritance slope (mg per mg)", q(1 + d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miDOC_input_z / cmp$s_up), q(d2$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input),
  "Macrophytes",         q(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_mimacrophy_abun_z),  q(d2$bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z),
  "Phytoplankton",       q(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miplankton_abun_z),  q(d2$bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z),
  "Soil litter cover",   q(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_micover_litter_z),   q(d2$bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z),
  "Water residence time",q(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miwater_res_time_z), q(d2$bsp_DOCout_miwater_res_time_z),
  "Between-stream SD",   q(d1$sd_site__deltaDOC_Intercept),     q(d2$sd_site__DOCout_Intercept),
  "Residual scale σ",    q(d1$sigma_deltaDOC),                  q(d2$sigma_DOCout),
  "Degrees of freedom ν",q(d1$nu_deltaDOC),                     q(d2$nu_DOCout),
  "Average ΔDOC (delta_SCM intercept; downstream_DOC evaluated at mean upstream DOC)",
     q(d1$b_deltaDOC_Intercept), q(d2$b_DOCout_Intercept + (d2$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input - 1) * cmp$mu_up)))
```

A further check: fixing the inheritance slope at exactly 1 (so that @eq-subtract has no upstream term at all — the pure paired contrast) leaves every mediator effect inside its credible interval (`analysis_plan.qmd`, section 4). The mediator story does not depend on how upstream DOC is handled.

# 3. Does the propagation of the measurement error differ, and does it matter?

The two models treat the 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ instrument error differently, and this is a real difference, not a relabelling:

-   **delta_SCM** propagates both errors into the outcome: $\Delta\text{DOC}$ carries $\sqrt{0.2^2 + 0.2^2} = 0.283$ mg L$^{-1}$ (`mi(0.283)`), and upstream DOC enters as a standardized predictor without error.
-   **downstream_DOC** carries only the downstream error on the outcome (`mi(0.2)`) and treats upstream DOC as a predictor measured without error (its `mi()` sub-model only imputes the 20 missing values). The 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ error of upstream DOC is therefore *not* propagated as an errors-in-variables term.

In principle an error on a predictor attenuates its slope toward zero by the reliability ratio $\text{var}(\text{true}) / (\text{var}(\text{true}) + 0.2^2)$. With an upstream-DOC standard deviation of `r sprintf("%.2f", cmp$s_up)` mg L$^{-1}$, that ratio is `r sprintf("%.3f", cmp$s_up^2 / (cmp$s_up^2 + 0.04))`: the inheritance slope could be understated by about `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - cmp$s_up^2 / (cmp$s_up^2 + 0.04)))`, i.e. 0.95 might be 0.96. The mediator effects are unaffected. We tested the fully propagated version (upstream DOC as a latent `me(up, 0.2)` predictor with a free slope) in a two-equation pilot: with two samplings per stream and a stream random effect it is weakly identified (slope 0.44 with an interval spanning most of the plausible range, R-hat above 1.01), so it is not usable, and the 1% attenuation it would correct is far below any other uncertainty in the model (`scm_rebuild.qmd`, section 3).

**So: the propagation differs, and it does not matter here** — the differences between the two columns of @tbl-equivalence are at the third decimal, and they come from exactly this (0.2 versus 0.283 on the outcome) plus the prior scale of the upstream coefficient, both changed on purpose. A reader who wants ΔDOC's error propagated exactly has it in delta_SCM; a reader who wants the inheritance reading has it in downstream_DOC, at the price of an attenuation of about one percent on one coefficient.

# 4. Pros and cons

**delta_SCM — ΔDOC as the outcome**

-   *Pro:* models the process of interest directly; the outcome *is* the local change.
-   *Pro:* the measurement error of both concentrations is propagated exactly into the outcome.
-   *Pro:* it is the model already described in the Methods of the current draft (Equation eq:scm), with priors, checks and Appendix S1 figures built around it.
-   *Con:* upstream DOC plays two roles, as a predictor and as half of the outcome; the coefficient $\beta_1$ then mixes "inheritance below one" with "retention", and the manuscript's original wording ("high upstream DOC causes greater retention") is the misreading this invites.
-   *Con:* the intercept is the average ΔDOC, so the model says nothing directly about how much of downstream DOC is simply carried over from upstream.

**downstream_DOC — downstream DOC as the outcome**

-   *Pro:* one role for upstream DOC; the inheritance slope (0.95 mg per mg) is a directly interpretable, reportable number.
-   *Pro:* the mediators read as what beaver-engineering *adds* to an inherited state — the same sentence on which $S$, $R_s$ and $G$ (Q3) and the spatial-coherence result (regional signal, local modification) are built.
-   *Pro:* ΔDOC is recovered for every stream and draw, with its seasonal averages reproducing Q1 (@fig-ddoc), so the process view is not lost.
-   *Con:* the upstream error is not propagated as an errors-in-variables term (about 1% attenuation on the inheritance slope, section 3).
-   *Con:* ΔDOC becomes a derived quantity; a reader who wants "the model of the local change" has to follow one subtraction.
-   *Con:* it requires re-describing the Methods equation and re-drawing Figure 1b.

**Recommendation.** Report downstream_DOC as the SCM of the manuscript, and state in one Methods sentence that it is the ΔDOC model of Equation eq:scm in a reparameterization, that the two agree to the second decimal, and that the upstream error would attenuate the inheritance slope by at most about one percent. This keeps the exact-propagation argument available and lets the paper lead with the reading it needs.

# 5. The story the downstream-DOC reading tells

Josh's argument for the reparameterization was not statistical but narrative, and it is worth stating because it decides the choice. With downstream DOC as the outcome, the manuscript's three results become one sentence with three clauses:

1.  **A stream inherits a DOC signal from its corridor** — downstream DOC is 95% upstream DOC, and the inherited seasonal contrast $S$ is regionally coherent (spatial coherence 0.48 with the 8 nearest neighbours).
2.  **Beaver-engineering modifies that inherited signal locally** — through light, primary producers and litter (the SCM); the modification $B$ is spatially incoherent (−0.04), i.e. each stream modifies the regional signal on its own terms.
3.  **The modification is a fraction of the inherited signal and redistributes it** — in summer beaver-engineering adds about a fifth of the inherited seasonal contrast ($R_{summer}$ = 0.21), and stream by stream it reinforces (43%), dampens (37%) or reverses (21%) that contrast ($G$).

Under the ΔDOC reading, clause 1 has no natural place: the model's intercept is an average change and the upstream coefficient is a "retention" effect, so the inherited signal that clauses 2 and 3 modify never appears as a quantity. Under the downstream reading, the SCM supplies the inherited state (the slope), Q3 measures the modification relative to it, and the spatial analysis says where each lives. That is the reason to prefer it — provided the reader is told, as above, that it is the same model.

# 6. Why keep upstream DOC as a separate term? {#sec-upstream}

Because it is the one variable in the system that beaver-engineering cannot cause, and the manuscript's argument needs it as a quantity, not as something folded into the outcome.

-   **It is the exogenous incoming state.** Upstream DOC is measured above the first dam; the placebo test shows the beaver-engineering variables do not predict it (`analysis_plan.qmd`, section 9 C). It is therefore the natural baseline against which the local modification is defined — the "inherited state" of Josh's framing.
-   **Folding it into ΔDOC assumes the inheritance slope is exactly 1.** $\Delta\text{DOC} = \text{DOC}_{down} - 1 \times \text{DOC}_{up}$ fixes the coefficient of upstream DOC at one by construction. Keeping it separate lets the data estimate it (0.95 [0.92, 0.98]) — and the robustness check that fixes it at 1 shows the mediators do not depend on the choice, so nothing is risked by estimating it.
-   **Kept separate, it becomes a result.** "Downstream DOC carries 95% of upstream DOC" is a reportable number; the seasonal change of upstream DOC is $S$, the inherited seasonal contrast, on which $R_s$ and $G$ are defined; and in the pathway decomposition the inheritance shortfall $(\beta_{inh} - 1)\,\text{DOC}_{up}$ turns out to be the largest single component separating sinks from sources (streams receiving the most DOC are the ones that deplete). None of this is visible if upstream DOC lives inside the outcome.
-   **Kept separate, it has one role.** In b1 it is both subtracted inside the outcome and used as a predictor; the coefficient then reads as "retention", which is the misreading of the current draft (section 4).
-   **What it costs.** The 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ error of upstream DOC is then not propagated into the outcome (section 3): about 1% attenuation on the inheritance slope, nothing on the mediators.

# 7. Does the model predict downstream DOC? {#sec-ppc}

Out-of-sample check by Pareto-smoothed importance-sampling leave-one-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO): for each observed downstream concentration, the prediction is made *as if that observation had been left out of the fit*. Metrics on the `r length(obs)` observed downstream concentrations:

```{r loo-table}
#| echo: false
lm <- P$loo_metrics; r2 <- P$r2_in
k <- P$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k
kable(tribble(
  ~Metric, ~Value,
  "In-sample Bayes R² (posterior mean [95% CrI])", sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", r2[1, "Estimate"], r2[1, "Q2.5"], r2[1, "Q97.5"]),
  "LOO R² (leave-one-out predictive mean vs observed)", sprintf("%.2f", lm["R2_loo"]),
  "LOO RMSE (mg L⁻¹)", sprintf("%.2f", lm["RMSE_loo"]),
  "Coverage of the 90% LOO predictive interval", sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * lm["cover90"]),
  "PSIS-LOO ELPD (SE)", sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", P$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"], P$loo$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"]),
  "Pareto k > 0.7 (observations with unreliable LOO)", sprintf("%d of %d", sum(k > 0.7), length(k))),
  caption = "Predictive performance of the downstream-DOC SCM for downstream DOC. The hold-out test on unseen streams (R² 0.84, 90% coverage 87%) is in analysis_plan.qmd, section 8.")
```

```{r fig-ppc}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**Downstream DOC: predicted vs observed.** (a) Leave-one-out predictive mean of downstream DOC against the observed concentration, one point per sampling; vertical segments: 90% LOO predictive interval; dashed line: 1:1. (b) Posterior predictive check: density of the observed downstream concentrations (dark) against 100 replicated datasets drawn from the model (light)."
y <- P$y; mu <- P$mu_loo; qq <- P$q_loo
pa <- ggplot(tibble(y, mu, lo = qq[1, ], hi = qq[2, ]), aes(y, mu)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "grey70", alpha = .6) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, colour = "#3B9AD1") +
  labs(x = expression("Observed downstream DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = expression("LOO-predicted downstream DOC (mg "*L^-1*")")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
pb <- ppc_dens_overlay(y, P$pp_sub[1:100, obs]) + xlim(0, 20) +
  labs(x = expression("Downstream DOC (mg "*L^-1*")")) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
pa + pb + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key message of @fig-ppc

-   Leave-one-out R² `r sprintf("%.2f", lm["R2_loo"])`, RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", lm["RMSE_loo"])` mg L$^{-1}$, 90% intervals covering `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * lm["cover90"])` of the observations; all Pareto $k$ below 0.7.
-   In-sample R² `r sprintf("%.2f", r2[1, "Estimate"])`: in and out of sample agree, so the model does not overfit; the R² is capped by a few very high concentrations that the Student-*t* likelihood deliberately does not chase.
-   **Implication.** The model reproduces downstream DOC at the level a survey model can, and almost all of that skill is inheritance.
:::

# 8. How ΔDOC is derived a posteriori {#sec-derived}

The model never sees ΔDOC. It is computed **after** fitting, once per posterior draw $d$ and sampling $i$, from two numbers the draw already contains — the predicted downstream concentration and the upstream concentration:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta\text{DOC}^{(d)}_i &= \mu^{(d)}_i - \text{DOC}_{up,i} \\
&= \alpha'^{(d)} + \left(\beta_{inh}^{(d)} - 1\right)\text{DOC}_{up,i} + \sum_k \beta'^{(d)}_k M_{k,i} + u'^{(d)}_{site(i)}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-derived}

(the 20 missing upstream values are the draw's imputed values). Doing this for all draws gives ΔDOC a full posterior distribution for every sampling, with no additional model. The seasonal average is the same operation averaged over the samplings of a season:

$$
\overline{\Delta\text{DOC}}^{(d)}_{s} = \frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i \in s} \Delta\text{DOC}^{(d)}_i
$$ {#eq-avg}

```{r fig-ddoc}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**ΔDOC recovered from the downstream-DOC model.** (a) Posterior median of the derived ΔDOC (@eq-derived) against the observed ΔDOC (downstream minus upstream reading) for every sampling with both concentrations measured; dashed line: 1:1. (b) Posterior distribution of the derived seasonal average ΔDOC (@eq-avg); point: median, bars: 66% and 95% credible intervals; the open diamonds are the seasonal averages of the Q1 paired-contrast model reported in the manuscript (+0.14 mg L⁻¹ summer, 0.00 winter)."
dm <- apply(P$dd_sub, 2, median)
pa <- ggplot(tibble(obs = P$d_obs, med = dm), aes(obs, med)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, colour = "#3B9AD1", alpha = .8) +
  labs(x = expression("Observed "*Delta*"DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = expression("Derived "*Delta*"DOC, posterior median (mg "*L^-1*")")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
av <- as_tibble(P$avg_season) |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "season", values_to = "v") |>
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels = c("winter", "summer")))
q1 <- tibble(season = factor(c("winter", "summer"), levels = c("winter", "summer")), v = c(0.00, 0.14))
pb <- ggplot(av, aes(v, season)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.66, .95), point_interval = "median_qi", fill = "grey80") +
  geom_point(data = q1, shape = 23, size = 3, fill = "white", colour = "#E8603C", stroke = 1.2) +
  labs(x = expression("Derived seasonal average "*Delta*"DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
pa + pb + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

```{r ddoc-metrics}
#| echo: false
dm2 <- P$ddoc_metrics
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key message of @fig-ddoc

-   The derived seasonal averages are `r sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median(P$avg_season[, "summer"]), quantile(P$avg_season[, "summer"], .025), quantile(P$avg_season[, "summer"], .975))` mg L$^{-1}$ in summer and `r sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median(P$avg_season[, "winter"]), quantile(P$avg_season[, "winter"], .025), quantile(P$avg_season[, "winter"], .975))` in winter, against +0.14 [0.05, 0.22] and 0.00 [−0.06, 0.07] from the Q1 model that uses the data alone — the same ordering and overlapping intervals, from two different models.
-   Sampling by sampling, the leave-one-out prediction of ΔDOC has RMSE `r sprintf("%.2f", dm2["RMSE_loo"])` mg L$^{-1}$ against `r sprintf("%.2f", dm2["RMSE_null"])` for predicting the grand mean (LOO R² `r sprintf("%.2f", dm2["R2_loo"])`): the local change is small relative to the inherited state and its sign is stream-specific.
-   **Implication.** Nothing about ΔDOC is lost by not making it the outcome; and no parameterization of this SCM predicts *which* stream will be a source or a sink — that is a property of the system (Q1), not of the model.
:::

# 9. Does the derived ΔDOC depend on the model specification? {#sec-spec}

Francesco's concern is right in general and it is worth answering in two parts: which ΔDOC the manuscript makes inference on, and what actually happens to the derived ΔDOC when the SCM changes.

**Part 1 — the manuscript never makes inference on the SCM's ΔDOC.** There are two different quantities called ΔDOC:

| | Where it comes from | Depends on the SCM's variables? | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ΔDOC from the data** | the paired-contrast measurement-error model on the raw upstream and downstream concentrations (Q1, Figure 1a), and the four-concentration model behind $S$, $R_s$, $B$, $G$ (Q3, Figure 2) — no mediators, no drivers | **no** | every inference on direction, magnitude and seasonal gain in the manuscript |
| **ΔDOC derived from the SCM** | $\mu_i - \text{DOC}_{up,i}$, the SCM's *expected* local modification given the drivers (@eq-derived) | **yes** — as any fitted value does | interpreting Q2: which pathways contribute (the decomposition), and the consistency checks in this document |

So the answer to "would it be better to model ΔDOC directly from the data?" is: **that is what the manuscript does, wherever it draws a conclusion about ΔDOC.** The SCM's derived ΔDOC is a fitted value, and fitted values always depend on the specification — but nothing about the direction, the average, the source/sink shares or $R_s$ rests on it.

**Part 2 — the concern applies identically to both parameterizations.** If the SCM had ΔDOC as its outcome (delta_SCM), adding or removing a variable would change its fitted ΔDOC, $\mu^{\Delta}_i$, in exactly the same way — because delta_SCM and downstream_DOC are one likelihood (@eq-subtract), $\mu^{\Delta}_i = \mu_i - \text{DOC}_{up,i}$ draw for draw. The choice of outcome does not create or remove the dependence on the specification; only the choice of variables does. That dependence is what section 9 of `analysis_plan.qmd` tests, and here is what it does to the derived ΔDOC itself:

```{r load-dag-ddoc}
#| echo: false
dd_path <- here("results", "derived_ddoc_by_dag.rds"); have_dd <- file.exists(dd_path)
if (have_dd) DD <- readRDS(dd_path)
```

```{r fig-spec}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**The derived ΔDOC under four SCM specifications.** DAG 0 is downstream_DOC; DAG 1 adds upstream DOC → producers; DAG 2 adds a direct solar → DOC path; DAG 3 adds season as a common cause of the producers and DOC (analysis_plan.qmd, section 9). (a) Posterior median of the derived ΔDOC of every sampling under each alternative DAG against DAG 0; dashed line: 1:1. (b) Derived seasonal average ΔDOC under each DAG; point: median, bars: 66% and 95% credible intervals; open diamonds: the Q1 model's averages, which come from the data alone (+0.14 summer, 0.00 winter)."
if (have_dd) {
  sc <- bind_rows(lapply(c("dag1","dag2","dag3"), function(nm) tibble(dag = gsub("dag", "DAG ", nm), d0 = DD$dag0$med, d = DD[[nm]]$med)))
  pa <- ggplot(sc, aes(d0, d, colour = dag)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
    geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = .7) + scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
    labs(x = expression("Derived "*Delta*"DOC, DAG 0 (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = expression("Derived "*Delta*"DOC, alternative DAG (mg "*L^-1*")")) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
  av <- bind_rows(lapply(names(DD), function(nm) as_tibble(DD[[nm]]$avg) |> mutate(dag = gsub("dag", "DAG ", nm)))) |>
    pivot_longer(c(summer, winter), names_to = "season", values_to = "v") |> mutate(season = factor(season, levels = c("winter", "summer")))
  q1 <- tibble(season = factor(c("winter", "summer"), levels = c("winter", "summer")), v = c(0, 0.14))
  pb <- ggplot(av, aes(x = v, y = season, colour = dag)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
    stat_pointinterval(.width = c(.66, .95), point_interval = "median_qi", position = position_dodge(width = .5)) +
    geom_point(data = q1, aes(x = v, y = season), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 23, size = 3, fill = "white", colour = "#E8603C", stroke = 1.2) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
    labs(x = expression("Derived seasonal average "*Delta*"DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
  pa + pb + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
} else cat("Not yet computed (notebook/R/derived_ddoc_by_dag.R).")
```

```{r spec-numbers}
#| echo: false
if (have_dd) {
  cors <- sapply(c("dag1","dag2","dag3"), function(nm) cor(DD$dag0$med, DD[[nm]]$med))
  mad  <- sapply(c("dag1","dag2","dag3"), function(nm) median(abs(DD$dag0$med - DD[[nm]]$med)))
  avs  <- sapply(names(DD), function(nm) median(DD[[nm]]$avg[, "summer"]))
  avw  <- sapply(names(DD), function(nm) median(DD[[nm]]$avg[, "winter"]))

```

::: {.callout-important}
## Answer to question 4

-   **Inference on ΔDOC is made from the data, not from the SCM.** Direction (Q1), magnitude and seasonal gain (Q3) come from measurement-error models on the raw concentrations that contain no drivers; changing the SCM cannot touch them.
-   **The derived ΔDOC is a fitted value and depends on the specification — equally under either parameterization,** because delta_SCM and downstream_DOC are the same likelihood; the outcome choice neither adds nor removes that dependence.
`r if (have_dd) sprintf("- **Empirically the dependence is small.** Across the four DAGs the per-sampling derived ΔDOC correlates at %s with DAG 0 (median absolute difference %s mg L⁻¹), and the derived seasonal averages are %s (summer) and %s (winter) against +0.14 and 0.00 from the data alone.", paste(sprintf("%.2f", cors), collapse = ", "), paste(sprintf("%.2f", mad), collapse = ", "), paste(sprintf("%.2f", avs), collapse = ", "), paste(sprintf("%.2f", avw), collapse = ", ")) else "- pending"`
-   **Implication.** What the SCM's ΔDOC is *for* — attributing the local modification to pathways — is exactly the use in which specification dependence is the object of study, and section 9 of the plan (alternative DAGs, confounding, priors) is where that dependence is reported. It is not a route by which a mis-specified SCM could bias the manuscript's claims about ΔDOC.
:::

# 10. What do we gain? The upstream → ΔDOC coefficient of delta_SCM {#sec-gain}

The most concrete gain is the meaning of one number. In delta_SCM the coefficient of upstream DOC on ΔDOC is `r sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", mean(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miDOC_input_z), quantile(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miDOC_input_z, .025), quantile(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miDOC_input_z, .975))` per SD of upstream DOC, i.e. `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(d1$bsp_deltaDOC_miDOC_input_z) / cmp$s_up)` mg of ΔDOC per mg of upstream DOC. What does it mean?

-   Read literally, "more upstream DOC causes a more negative ΔDOC" — the current draft called this *retention*, as if the pond removed a fixed fraction of what enters. But ΔDOC contains −DOC$_{up}$ by construction, so the coefficient mixes two things: how much of the inflow is passed on, and any genuine removal that scales with the inflow. The number alone cannot separate them; it is not even clear whether a *negative* value is a finding or an artefact of the subtraction.
-   In downstream_DOC the same information is the inheritance slope, 0.95 [0.92, 0.98] mg per mg: *downstream DOC carries 95% of the upstream concentration*. That is unambiguous, it has units a reader understands, and its distance from 1 (5%) is the net shortfall — which is where any inflow-scaled removal must live. It is the same estimate (@eq-subtract), stated in a way that cannot be misread.

The other gains follow from that one:

-   the inherited state becomes a quantity the rest of the paper uses ($S$, $R_s$, $G$, the spatial-coherence result, the pathway decomposition);
-   upstream DOC has one role instead of two (@sec-upstream);
-   Francesco's own hypothesis (@sec-francesco-dag) — that the inflow modulates the beaver modification through the producers — can be written as an indirect effect of upstream DOC, which in delta_SCM would be an indirect effect of a variable that also sits inside the outcome.

What we do **not** gain: fit, mediator estimates, or the propagation of the upstream error (section 3). If Francesco prefers delta_SCM for Q2, the paper loses nothing statistically; it loses the inheritance number and the clean reading of the upstream coefficient.

# 11. Francesco's DAG: upstream DOC → producers, plus the direct link {#sec-francesco-dag}

This is exactly DAG 1 of the structural-sensitivity analysis (`analysis_plan.qmd`, section 9), fitted with the downstream_DOC parameterization plus two arrows: upstream DOC → phytoplankton and upstream DOC → macrophytes. The inflow then reaches downstream DOC by three routes — directly (inheritance) and through each producer — and "the baseline modulates the beaver modification through the producers" is the **indirect effect** of upstream DOC.

```{r load-dag1}
#| echo: false
D1 <- readRDS(here("results", "dag1_effects.rds")); tb <- D1$tab; dd1 <- D1$draws
gv <- function(par) tb[tb$par == par, ]
```

```{r fig-francesco-dag}
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-cap: "**Francesco's DAG (DAG 1): upstream DOC drives the primary producers as well as downstream DOC.** Posterior mean effects from the fitted model; the two added paths are in dark red, in units of standardized producer abundance per mg L⁻¹ of upstream DOC; the upstream → downstream path is the inheritance slope (mg per mg); the others are standardized effects as in Figure 1b. Solid: posterior probability of the sign above 0.90; dashed grey: no-evidence."
nodes <- data.frame(name = c("Max dam\nheight", "Number of\ndams", "Channel\ngradient", "Water\nresidence time", "Solar\nradiation", "Macrophytes", "Phytoplankton", "Soil litter\ncover", "Upstream\nDOC", "Downstream\nDOC"),
  x = c(0.9, 0.9, 2.9, 3.2, 4.6, 6.6, 6.2, 6.2, 8.8, 8.8), y = c(6.6, 4.6, 2.0, 5.0, 9.3, 7.2, 5.0, 2.9, 8.8, 5.4))
rownames(nodes) <- c("dh", "nd", "gr", "wrt", "sol", "mac", "pla", "lit", "up", "out")
ed <- function(from, to, par, curv = 0, lx = 0, ly = 0.3, new = FALSE) { g <- gv(par)
  tibble(from = from, to = to, label = sprintf("%.2f", g$mean), class = if (new) "new" else if (g$p_pos > 0.9) "pos" else if (g$p_pos < 0.1) "neg" else "none",
         solid = g$p_pos > 0.9 | g$p_pos < 0.1, curv = curv, lx = lx, ly = ly) }
edges <- bind_rows(
  ed("dh", "wrt", "bsp_waterrestimez_midam_height_z"), ed("nd", "wrt", "b_waterrestimez_n_dams_z", lx = -0.1, ly = 0.35),
  ed("gr", "wrt", "b_waterrestimez_slope_z", lx = 0.45, ly = 0), ed("wrt", "pla", "bsp_planktonabunz_miwater_res_time_z"),
  ed("wrt", "mac", "bsp_macrophyabunz_miwater_res_time_z"), ed("wrt", "out", "bsp_DOCout_miwater_res_time_z", curv = 0.18),
  ed("sol", "mac", "bsp_macrophyabunz_misolar_z", curv = -0.15, lx = 0.55, ly = 0.55), ed("sol", "pla", "bsp_planktonabunz_misolar_z", curv = 0.30, lx = -0.85, ly = 0.1),
  ed("sol", "lit", "bsp_coverlitterz_misolar_z", curv = 0.30), ed("mac", "out", "bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z", ly = 0.32),
  ed("pla", "out", "bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z", ly = 0.30), ed("lit", "out", "bsp_DOCout_micover_litter_z", lx = -0.2, ly = 0.32),
  ed("up", "out", "bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input", lx = 0.45, ly = 0),
  ed("up", "mac", "bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input", curv = 0.25, lx = 0.35, ly = 0.35, new = TRUE),
  ed("up", "pla", "bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input", curv = -0.35, lx = -0.9, ly = -0.9, new = TRUE))
edges$label[!edges$solid & edges$class != "new"] <- ""
a <- merge(edges, nodes, by.x = "from", by.y = "row.names"); a <- merge(a, nodes, by.x = "to", by.y = "row.names", suffixes = c("", "2"))
dx <- a$x2 - a$x; dy <- a$y2 - a$y; L <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
a$x0 <- a$x + dx / L * 0.85; a$y0 <- a$y + dy / L * 0.55; a$x1 <- a$x2 - dx / L * 0.90; a$y1 <- a$y2 - dy / L * 0.55
a$xm <- (a$x0 + a$x1) / 2 + a$lx; a$ym <- (a$y0 + a$y1) / 2 + a$ly
pal <- c(pos = "#3B9AD1", neg = "#E8603C", none = "grey55", new = "#8B0000"); arr <- arrow(length = unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed")
pd <- ggplot()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(a))) { lt <- if (a$class[i] == "new") (if (a$solid[i]) "solid" else "dotted") else if (a$solid[i]) "solid" else "dashed"
  pd <- pd + if (a$curv[i] == 0) geom_segment(data = a[i, ], aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), colour = pal[a$class[i]], linetype = lt, linewidth = 0.7, arrow = arr) else
    geom_curve(data = a[i, ], aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), curvature = a$curv[i], colour = pal[a$class[i]], linetype = lt, linewidth = 0.7, arrow = arr) }
pd <- pd + geom_text(data = subset(a, label != ""), aes(x = xm, y = ym, label = label, colour = class), size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(pos = "black", neg = "black", none = "black", new = "#8B0000")) +
  geom_label(data = nodes[rownames(nodes) != "out", ], aes(x = x, y = y, label = name), size = 4, label.padding = unit(0.3, "lines"), label.r = unit(0.05, "lines")) +
  geom_label(data = nodes["out", ], aes(x = x, y = y, label = name), size = 4.3, fontface = "bold", label.padding = unit(0.45, "lines"), label.r = unit(0.9, "lines"), linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#C0208E") +
  xlim(0, 10) + ylim(1.2, 10) + theme_void()
ggsave(here("results", "figures", "plan", "fig_francesco_dag.png"), pd, width = 9, height = 5.6, dpi = 300, bg = "white"); pd
```

```{r dag1-effects}
#| echo: false
# effect of upstream DOC on downstream DOC and on dDOC, in mg per mg, per posterior draw
direct   <- dd1[, "bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input"]
ind_mac  <- dd1[, "bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input"] * dd1[, "bsp_DOCout_mimacrophy_abun_z"]
ind_pla  <- dd1[, "bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input"] * dd1[, "bsp_DOCout_miplankton_abun_z"]
indirect <- ind_mac + ind_pla; total <- direct + indirect
on_delta <- total - 1
qf <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", median(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
eff <- tibble(effect = c("direct (inheritance)", "indirect via macrophytes", "indirect via phytoplankton", "indirect, total", "total on downstream DOC", "total on ΔDOC (= total − 1)"),
              v = list(direct, ind_mac, ind_pla, indirect, total, on_delta)) |>
  mutate(med = sapply(v, median), lo = sapply(v, quantile, .025), hi = sapply(v, quantile, .975), p_pos = sapply(v, function(x) mean(x > 0)))
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Answer to question 7 (Francesco's DAG)

-   **The structure is supported for macrophytes, not for phytoplankton.** Upstream DOC → macrophytes `r sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f], P(> 0) = %.2f", gv("bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input")$mean, gv("bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input")$lo, gv("bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input")$hi, gv("bsp_macrophyabunz_miDOC_input")$p_pos)` SD per mg L⁻¹; upstream DOC → phytoplankton `r sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f], P(> 0) = %.2f", gv("bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")$mean, gv("bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")$lo, gv("bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")$hi, gv("bsp_planktonabunz_miDOC_input")$p_pos)`. The mediator → DOC effects are unchanged (max R-hat `r sprintf("%.3f", D1$rhat)`).
-   **The indirect effect of the inflow through the producers is tiny.** `r qf(indirect)` mg per mg (macrophytes `r qf(ind_mac)`, phytoplankton `r qf(ind_pla)`), against a direct inheritance of `r qf(direct)`. Total on downstream DOC `r qf(total)`; on ΔDOC `r qf(on_delta)` — the net shortfall of about 5% is not compensated by the producer route.
-   **Implication.** Francesco's hypothesis — the baseline modulates the beaver modification through the producers — is testable in this parameterization and, on these data, the modulation runs through macrophytes and is an order of magnitude smaller than the direct shortfall: the more DOC comes in, the more negative ΔDOC becomes (`r sprintf("%.3f", median(on_delta))` mg per mg), and the producers do not reverse that. With the producers measured at 16 summer streams, the indirect path is prior-informed (section 9 of the plan); the direct one rests on all streams.
:::

# 12. Our target is ΔDOC, not downstream DOC — and what the figures should show {#sec-target}

Francesco is right about the target, and the parameterization does not change it. Three points:

-   **The estimand is the local modification.** Every effect in downstream_DOC — the mediator coefficients, the derived ΔDOC, the pathway decomposition — is an effect on the local modification $\mu_i - \text{DOC}_{up,i}$, identical draw for draw to the fitted ΔDOC of delta_SCM (@eq-subtract). Downstream DOC is the *response* of the likelihood, not the object of inference; "beaver-engineering's effect on downstream DOC" and "on ΔDOC" are the same set of coefficients, except for the one on upstream DOC, which differs by exactly 1.
-   **"How the delta changes with the input" is one coefficient, and it is estimated, not hidden.** The expectation Francesco states — the more DOC enters, the more the beaver system dampens or amplifies — is the slope of ΔDOC on upstream DOC: $\beta_{inh} - 1$ = `r sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", median(d2$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input - 1), quantile(d2$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input - 1, .025), quantile(d2$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input - 1, .975))` mg per mg (dampening: the delta falls as the input rises), plus the producer route of @sec-francesco-dag. That is delta_SCM's $\beta_1$, now with units and a reading. @fig-target shows it on the data.
-   **The figures.** The figure that presents the SCM (Figure 1b, and @fig-francesco-dag) has downstream DOC as its outcome node, because that is what the model predicts; the predicted-vs-observed check (@fig-ppc) is on downstream DOC for the same reason. Every result figure — direction (Figure 1a), $R_s$ and $G$ (Figure 2), the decomposition — is on ΔDOC or on quantities built from it, because that is the target. And @fig-target is the figure Francesco is asking for: the delta as a function of the input.

```{r fig-target}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "**The local modification as a function of the input.** Derived ΔDOC of every sampling (posterior median, from downstream_DOC) against the observed upstream DOC; black line and band: the model's expected ΔDOC at the mean of the mediators, α + (β_inh − 1)·DOC_up, posterior median and 95% credible interval; dashed: zero. Right: the same on a logarithmic x axis. The negative slope is delta_SCM's β₁ in mg per mg: the more DOC comes in, the lower the delta — the beaver system dampens a rich inflow."
dm <- apply(P$dd_sub, 2, median); up <- P$dat$DOC_input[P$both]
grid <- seq(min(up), max(up), length.out = 80)
line <- sapply(grid, function(u) d2$b_DOCout_Intercept + (d2$bsp_DOCout_miDOC_input - 1) * u)
ln <- tibble(up = grid, med = apply(line, 2, median), lo = apply(line, 2, quantile, .025), hi = apply(line, 2, quantile, .975))
base <- ggplot(tibble(up, dm), aes(up, dm)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_ribbon(data = ln, aes(x = up, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "black", alpha = .15) +
  geom_line(data = ln, aes(up, med), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.3, colour = "#3B9AD1", alpha = .8) +
  labs(x = expression("Upstream DOC (mg "*L^-1*")"), y = expression("Derived "*Delta*"DOC, posterior median (mg "*L^-1*")")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
base + (base + scale_x_log10()) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

# 13. The pipeline in one picture

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "From the four measured concentrations to the quantities reported in the manuscript. The SCM (Q2) predicts downstream DOC; ΔDOC is derived from its posterior. Q1 and Q3 use the concentrations directly through their own measurement-error models."
flowchart LR
  A["Measured per stream and season:<br/>DOC upstream, DOC downstream<br/>(0.2 mg/L instrument error)"] --> Q1
  A --> SCM
  A --> Q3
  M["Mediators (16 streams):<br/>producers, litter, residence time,<br/>solar radiation, dams"] --> SCM
  Q1["Q1 paired-contrast model<br/>outcome: ΔDOC per sampling"] --> F1["Figure 1a<br/>direction, ROPE"]
  SCM["Q2 structural causal model<br/>outcome: downstream DOC<br/>upstream DOC = inherited state (β = 0.95)"] --> Pp["Posterior draws:<br/>β, mediators, u_site"]
  Pp --> F1b["Figure 1b<br/>drivers"]
  Pp --> D["Derived per draw:<br/>ΔDOC = predicted downstream − upstream"]
  D --> CHK["Predicted vs observed,<br/>seasonal averages (this document)"]
  Q3["Q3 measurement-error model<br/>per concentration, per stream"] --> DV["Derived per draw:<br/>S, ΔDOC_s, R_s, B, G"]
  DV --> F2["Figure 2<br/>relative response, seasonal gain"]
```
